authoredSolutions.51: Each term is \((x+2k-2)(x+2k)\). Summing \(k=1\) to \(n\) and dividing by \(n\) gives \(x^2+2nx+\frac{4n^2-12}{3}=\frac{8}{3}\), i.e. \(x^2+2nx+\frac{4n^2-12}{3}=0\) after moving \(\frac{8n}{3}\) over. For two consecutive even roots the difference is \(2\): \((\alpha-\beta)^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-4\alpha\beta=4n^2-\frac{4(4n^2-12)}{3}=4\Rightarrow -4n^2+48=12\Rightarrow n^2=9\Rightarrow n=3.\)
authoredSolutions.52: Let \(u=\tan^2x-2\tan x+a=(\tan x-1)^2+(a-1)\ge a-1\). Since \(f''>0\), \(f'\) is increasing with \(f'(a-1)=0\), so \(f'(u)\ge 0\). Also \(u'=2(\tan x-1)\sec^2x\). On \((0,\tfrac{\pi}{4})\), \(\tan x<1\Rightarrow u'<0\Rightarrow g'=f'(u)u'<0\): \(g\) is decreasing, so (I) is false. On \((\tfrac{\pi}{4},\tfrac{\pi}{2})\), \(u'>0\Rightarrow g'>0\): \(g\) is increasing, so (II) is false. Neither is true.
